title: Universal Emergence of Bosonic and Fermionic Algebras in a Deterministic Proper-Time Framework
abstract: This work develops the deterministic, discrete proper-time framework introduced in our previous work, Eur.\ Phys.\ J.\ C \textbf{86} (2026) 829, in which quantum field theory emerges as an effective infrared description characterized by a running Planck constant. There, the effective quantization scale was inferred from the microscopic multiplicity unresolved by coarse-graining. Here, we provide its dynamical and operatorial realization and extend the construction to fermionic degrees of freedom. First, consistency under changes of macroscopic resolution leads to the structure of the Renormalization Group Equation, while the running Planck constant governs the crossover toward the deterministic regime. Second, we represent the reversible microscopic dynamics through finite-difference translations in field-configuration space. After coarse-graining, the resulting operator-valued canonical commutation relations reproduce the same quantization scale previously obtained from statistical microstate counting, thereby linking microscopic evolution to the emergent canonical algebra. Third, representing the same update within a Grassmann algebra yields the corresponding canonical anticommutation relations. The bosonic and fermionic sectors thus inherit a common effective Planck constant without introducing an independent fermionic update or quantization scale. Finally, we discuss possible implications for high-energy loop amplitudes and effective Hawking radiation.
summary: This paper proposes a deterministic framework where Quantum Field Theory emerges from discrete, microscopic proper-time evolution. It rigorously constructs both bosonic and fermionic commutation/anticommutation relations using this underlying dynamics. The key achievement is demonstrating that both sectors share a common effective Planck constant, suggesting a unified origin for quantum statistics.
main_problem: The work develops a deterministic, discrete proper-time framework aiming to explain how Quantum Field Theory (QFT) emerges as an effective infrared description.
main_result: It successfully shows that both bosonic and fermionic sectors inherit a common effective Planck constant ($\hbar_{	ext{eff}}$) derived from the underlying microscopic dynamics, linking canonical algebra emergence to unresolved microstate counting.
method: The methodology involves analyzing consistency under resolution changes to derive Renormalization Group structure, using finite-difference translations for bosons, and employing Grassmann algebras for fermions.
model_or_system: The model is a deterministic, discrete proper-time framework built on ordered event chains. QFT emerges as the coarse-grained limit of this underlying microscopic evolution.
key_observables: Effective running Planck constant ($\hbar_{	ext{eff}}$), bosonic commutation relations, fermionic anticommutation relations, and Hawking radiation suppression factors.
important_parameters: The effective quantization scale derived from unresolved microscopic multiplicity ($n_\mu$), the minimal proper time interval ($	au_{\min}$), and the resolution parameter ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: QFT is treated as an effective infrared description resulting from coarse-graining over fundamental deterministic histories, and the framework assumes a common underlying update mechanism for both particle types.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the RGE structure via resolution changes, then deriving bosonic canonical relations using finite differences, extending this to fermions via Grassmann algebra, and finally discussing implications like Hawking radiation suppression.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, its focus on emergent quantization scales ($\hbar_{	ext{eff}}$) and linking fundamental dynamics (deterministic updates) to established quantum structures (RGE, canonical algebras) provides a novel perspective on the foundations of QFT relevant to open systems theory.
